Market hall reopens with forty stalls after its restoration

Words by Priya Lindqvist · 19 October 2026

Key points, every Friday

  • The week's five biggest local stories in one short email.
  • Openings, closures and events across the town, before the weekend.
  • No adverts, and you can stop it in one click at any time.

Ashcombe's covered market hall opened again on Saturday after eighteen months of restoration, with forty stalls selling bread, cheese, fish, flowers and secondhand books under its iron and glass roof.

The hall was built in 1889 and had been closed since engineers found rust in the columns that hold up the roof. Each column was taken down, cleaned and strengthened in a workshop outside the town, then put back in its original place.

Most of the traders who left during the closure have come back, and a dozen new ones have joined them, among them a coffee roaster, a pasta maker and a stall that repairs bicycles while their owners do the shopping.

Rents for the first year have been frozen at the level they were before the closure, which the market's manager, Dorota Keane, said was the main reason so many stallholders had returned. "They waited for us, so we wanted to look after them," she said.

The restoration cost six and a half million pounds, shared between the town council and a heritage grant. The glass in the roof has been replaced with panes that let in more light and keep the hall warmer in winter.

Shoppers on the first morning were greeted by a brass band from the secondary school and by the town crier, who read out the original rules of the market from 1889, including a fine of one shilling for selling fish after noon in summer.

The market will open from eight until four on Tuesdays, Fridays and Saturdays, with a late opening until nine on the first Friday of every month, when the stalls will be joined by street food and live music.
